title: Yara and the Scholarship
premise: When sixteen-year-old Xanthe Eriksen moves to Hollow Creek, she discovers her grandmother's recipe box holds more than cards — hidden among them are instructions for the Scholarship, a century-old bargain in which the town's founders traded their memories to something beneath the school for prosperity. The Scholarship is due for renewal, and the 'payment' has quietly shifted from memories to the town's teenagers, who have been forgetting themselves one by one. Xanthe must gather the descendants of the founding families, uncover what her grandmother sacrificed, and rewrite the bargain before the solstice — ending with her dissolving the Scholarship entirely by returning every stolen memory, at the cost of her own recollection of the found family she built, which they promise to give back to her, one story at a time.
about_author: Rafael Delacroix is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records across the American Midwest, where he first heard stories of bargains towns make and never mention. He writes young adult fiction about kids who inherit debts they never signed for.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Arriving in Hollow Creek with her grieving mother, Xanthe catalogs every rule of being the new kid: don't draw attention, don't explain the scar, don't mention the years of therapy. She notices the town is oddly quiet about its own history. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness masking a fierce longing to belong somewhere.

chapters.title: The School on the Foundation
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. First day at Hollow Creek High, a building that sits oddly deep in the ground, its basement older than the town charter. A student named Dev warns her, jokingly, never to go into the sub-basement during finals week. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity; the school feels like it's listening.

chapters.title: Grandma's Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sorting her late grandmother's belongings, Xanthe finds a recipe box where several cards aren't recipes at all — they're instructions in her grandmother's handwriting: names, dates, and a phrase, 'Feed the Foundation before the solstice.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion that her grandmother hid a whole life from her.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Forgot Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A popular senior, Marisol, blankly introduces herself three times in one afternoon and later can't remember her little brother's birthday. Teachers shrug it off. Xanthe recognizes the hollow look from her own worst year. Emotional beat: dread — this isn't grief or drugs; something is taking pieces of people.

chapters.title: Dev and the Sub-Basement Key
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, the janitor's grandson, reveals his family has held the sub-basement key for four generations and that his grandfather died muttering about 'the interest coming due.' He shows Xanthe the door, warm to the touch in winter. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two careful kids recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Founders Traded
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Dev's alternating POV. In the town archive they find the founding charter's missing page: the Scholarship, a bargain granting Hollow Creek a century of good fortune in exchange for the founders' memories, renewed each generation. Emotional beat: the thrill of a real mystery colliding with horror that their town was built on a debt.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The recipe cards list six founding-family names; Xanthe and Dev track down the living descendants — Marisol among them. Most refuse to listen; one, prickly Theo Vance, confirms his family's 'luck' and their collective amnesia about the 1950s. Emotional beat: the fragile, messy beginning of a found family forged by a secret.

chapters.title: Solstice Is in Three Weeks
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Deciphering the cards' dates, they realize the renewal is due at the solstice — three weeks away — and that this time the Foundation is taking payment early, in installments: Marisol, then a freshman, then a teacher. Emotional beat: panic and resolve; the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Xanthe's Own Missing Year
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cross-referencing her therapy records, Xanthe realizes the 'accident' she's never fully remembered happened in Hollow Creek as a four-year-old — her grandmother paid something to save her, and the missing year is the receipt. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition; she was always part of this.

chapters.title: The First Descent
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Dev, and Theo's POV. They open the sub-basement and find a stairwell older than the school descending to a chamber of shelves — thousands of labeled jars, each holding a memory in amber light. Something vast and patient stirs below. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the scale of the theft made physical.

chapters.title: Marisol's Jar
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Guided by the others, Marisol finds her own jar and, touching it, floods back her stolen months — then collapses as the Foundation notices the theft. They barely escape. Emotional beat: the first victory, purchased with the knowledge that they've alerted the thing below.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets on Purpose
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The adults they confide in — including Xanthe's mother — react with eerie calm, then can't recall the conversation. Xanthe realizes the whole town is complicit, conditioned by generations of small surrenders. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into defiance; the kids can trust no one over thirty.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's family 'luck' curdles: his father, a founding descendant, offers to pay the Foundation with Theo's memories to protect the family business. Theo, betrayed, goes missing the night before the solstice. Emotional beat: rage and guilt — the found family's first fracture.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Card
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A final recipe card, hidden in the box's false bottom, reveals her grandmother's plan from decades ago: a way to dissolve the Scholarship — return every memory at once — but it requires a descendant willing to act as the conduit and lose their own memories in the exchange. Emotional beat: understanding her grandmother's sacrifice and the shape of her own choice.

chapters.title: The Rescue in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dev and Marisol's POV. They descend again to find Theo before his payment completes, navigating shelves that rearrange to trap them, using Marisol's returned memories of the chamber as a map. Emotional beat: courage as a group act; no one escapes alone, and they all know it now.

chapters.title: The Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Foundation, speaking through the school's intercom and the town's PA system, offers Xanthe a deal: her grandmother's debt forgiven, her missing year restored, her mother's grief erased — if she delivers the other descendants as payment. Emotional beat: temptation aimed precisely at her oldest wounds.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Full group POV, braided. The night before the solstice, the five kids argue about the dissolution ritual: it might not work, and it will cost Xanthe everything she remembers of them. They choose it anyway, each adding their own memory to the conduit as ballast. Emotional beat: the found family fully formed — love stated plainly, before it may be forgotten.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the chamber, Xanthe opens every jar while the Foundation floods her with returned memories — the founders' centuries, the town's stolen years, her own missing childhood. The ritual teeters as she nearly drowns in what isn't hers. Emotional beat: the climax; identity as the thing she refuses to surrender.

chapters.title: The Foundation Fails
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The chamber collapses inward as the Scholarship inverts — the Foundation, built entirely from held memories, is dissolved by having to give them all back. The kids escape up a stairwell that is already becoming ordinary concrete. Emotional beat: cathartic release; the weight lifting off a hundred years of the town.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Xanthe wakes with no memory of the last two months — or of them. The others find her name in their own notebooks and photographs and begin, awkwardly, to tell her who she was to them. Emotional beat: bittersweet tenderness; love persisting past forgetting.

chapters.title: One Story at a Time
chapters.summary: Braided group POV. Over the following weeks, each friend takes a turn retelling their chapter of the story — Dev at the door, Marisol's jar, Theo's rescue — and fragments of Xanthe's memory flicker back, unbidden, like light through amber. Emotional beat: hope grounded in effort; memory rebuilt by community, not magic alone.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box, Refilled
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. On the first anniversary, Xanthe adds her own cards to her grandmother's box — not instructions for a bargain, but recipes for the meals the five of them share every solstice now, a new tradition with nothing owed. The school basement is just a basement. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; the family she chose, kept on purpose.
